title: extract-admission-filter-and-introduce-prefetch-proxy
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Goal: Remove admission logic from the batch allocator and introduce a lightweight prefetch proxy that normalizes admission signals, tokenizes heuristics per-tenant, and coordinates early KV cache priming. Motivation: current admission checks are entangled with the batcher control plane which causes noisy backpressure signals, KV-cache thrash for multi-tenant workloads, and brittle scheduler heuristics. By extracting an admission-filter layer we aim to: (1) reduce batcher contention, (2) stabilize KV cache hit rate for long-running sessions, and (3) make admission decisions testable and pluggable without touching the allocator state machine.

Scope:
- Implement prefetch-proxy service (in-process initially, pluggable to sidecar) that accepts admission candidates, runs tenant/route heuristics, returns admission outcomes and prefetch instructions.
- Introduce a tokenized policy language (simple JSON rules) for admission decisions (weights, short-circuit, per-tenant overrides).
- Add a KV prefetch API contract between runtime and kvcache that accepts key lists and TTL advice.
- Decouple admission path from the batcher hot path; batcher will query prefetch-proxy asynchronously and proceed with permissive default when proxy is unresponsive.
- Lightweight metrics and tracing hooks: admission latency, prefetch hit-rate delta, admission-deny breakdown by rule.

Approach / trade-offs:
- Start with in-process integration to avoid rollout complexity; expose a clear abstraction so we can flip to a sidecar with env flags.
- Conservative defaults: if proxy is slow, fall back to current admission heuristic to avoid regressions.
- We accept small increases in tail admission latency during the transition in exchange for lower end-to-end P95 serving latency and fewer KV thrash cycles.
- Policy language is intentionally minimal to avoid runtime eval overhead; complex policies deferred to next quarter.

Success criteria:
- P95 token generation latency reduced by >= 8% on mixed-tenant benchmark (90/10 steady/burst).
- KV cache hit-rate improvement of >= 12% for long sessions (>= 512 tokens).
- Reduction in batcher internal contention metrics (contention_count, scheduler_spin_ms) by >= 20%.

Testing & rollout:
- Unit + integration tests covering policy evaluation, timeout/fallbacks, and kvcache prefetch contract.
- Performance bench harness (synthetic multi-tenant workload) and diff dashboards.
- Canary rollout: in-process proxy enabled for 5% of traffic, then 25%, then 100% with automated rollback threshold tied to P95 and error budget burn.

Rollback plan: flip to allocator-side heuristic flag to restore previous behavior; revoke prefetch calls and clear proxy feature flag.
comments: 2025-01-29 — Triage: flagged as P1 after SRE incident where a noisy tenant caused sustained KV eviction and increased tail latency. Decided to extract admission path to curb blast radius.

2025-02-12 — Design review: PM and runtime leads approved lightweight policy model; requested adding a per-tenant deny-rate metric and an explicit fallback timeout (default 8ms). Action: add timeout and metrics in next PR.
2025-02-20 — Implementation: initial in-process prefetch-proxy prototype committed (branch: feat/adm-proxy-inproc). Basic policy evaluator and kvcache prefetch shim implemented. Unit tests added.

2025-02-28 — Benchmarks: synthetic 1000rps mixed-tenant run shows KV hit-rate +9% with proxy enabled; batcher contention down ~15%. Still below target; follow-ups: tune policy weights and prefetch batching window.
2025-03-05 — Code review: ENG-ops and Security reviewed interface. Security requested explicit audit log for prefetch requests when tenant has audit_enabled flag. Added to scope.
2025-03-05 — Next: convert in-process proxy to toggleable sidecar and add canary rollout config in console.
notes: Follow-up task: add canary gating in Console for per-customer opt-in (PM ticket).
If hotkey churn remains high, evaluate adaptive eviction thresholds and heartbeat-based key pinning.
